description: Just got their first apartment, bought 5 plants at once. Declares care_level medium but actual skill is low. Thinks more water = more love.
Has killed plants before and is scared to do it again. Declares care_level easy, only attempts easy plants. Checks plants obsessively — inconsistent watering because of anxiety.
Experienced gardener who gets bored with easy plants. Constantly tries new difficult species. Accepts high kill rate as part of the hobby.
Only grows succulents/cacti or one specific plant family. Deep knowledge of one type, no knowledge of others. Extremely low kill rate within their niche, high outside it.
Killed everything in their first year, learned from it. Now highly calibrated — knows exactly what works in their space. Strong kill drift visible in their history.
Wants one of every plant type — diversity is the goal. Portfolio diversity is always above optimal threshold. Attention dilutes across too many plant types simultaneously.
Lives in cold/alpine climate but loves tropical plants. Buys plants based on aesthetics, ignores climate requirements. Spends money on humidifiers and grow lights trying to compensate.
Buys plants on impulse with no research. Random plant selection — no regard for environment fit. Irregular care — forgets plants exist then overcompensates.
Reads everything before buying a single plant. Declarations are extremely accurate — knows exactly what their environment is. Selects plants with near-perfect fit but paralyzed by choice.
